servo: add event object for each device Use a device specific event object to track whether the device is disconnected. Before they all used the same event object, so if CCD disconnected all servo controls would wait not just ccd controls. For an interface to wait for a device it needs to return the vid, pid, and serialname in get_device_info. If the interface doesn't have get_device_info, then the control will not wait for the interface to be available. hci: Choose legacy advertising over extended advertising commands. Bluetooth 5.0 (Vol 2, Part E, section 3.1.1) disallows mixing of legacy and extended advertising commands. However, there is no command to explicitly choose which mode (legacy or extended) the host wants to use, but rather the first advertising command will determine whether legacy or extended advertising commands will be allowed for the rest of the controller's lifetime (until Reset). So we call an arbitrary read-only legacy advertising command very early to tell the controller that we want to use the legacy advertising commands instead of extended advertising commands. Without specifying legacy vs extended commands very early, we might hit an unexpected Command Disallowed later on. For example, LE Set Scan Parameters hits Command Disallowed error on Thunder Peak. BUG=chromium:982443 TEST=Manual scanning test on atlas (Thunder Peak). servo: micro + ccd on same instance. Note: This is a temporay hack as go/servoarch will provide the same functionality, however in this case we need this double feature earlier. Expect this to be gone with servoarch with the rest of postinit. This change adds a new layer to postinit to allow for servo micro and ccd on the same servo instance iff both micro and ccd are enumerated and on the same v4 hub.
